props.title: Obsessed

sections.content: Obsessed marked a modern revival of the "fatal attraction" psychological thriller subgenre, following the template established by Fatal Attraction (1987). The film stars Idris Elba as a successful executive whose life unravels when a temp worker (Ali Larter) becomes dangerously fixated on him, threatening his marriage to Sharon (Beyoncé). While criticized for its predictability, the film taps into primal fears about workplace harassment and marital trust, similar to earlier entries like Disclosure (1994) and The Crush (1993).

sections.content: The workplace thriller aspect of Obsessed connects it to a specific subset of stalker films that explore professional boundaries and power dynamics. Films like Secretary (2002) and Notes on a Scandal (2006) examine similar themes through more nuanced lenses. The casting of Beyoncé marked a significant moment, as the film deliberately played with racial dynamics absent from many earlier entries in the genre, though some critics argued it missed opportunities for deeper exploration.

The film's climactic confrontation between Sharon and Lisa follows a tradition of theatrical showdowns in female-centered thrillers, reminiscent of The Hand That Rocks the Cradle (1992) and Sleeping with the Enemy (1991). This "defending the household" trope appears repeatedly in domestic thrillers, though Obsessed updates it for contemporary audiences with modern office politics and technology. sections.content: The stalker thriller genre has evolved significantly since the 1980s, with films like Play Misty for Me (1971) setting early templates. Obsessed represents a transitional moment, bridging classic stalker narratives with modern concerns about workplace harassment and digital surveillance. Later films like Gone Girl (2014) and The Gift (2015) would further deconstruct these tropes, adding layers of unreliable narration and psychological complexity absent from earlier iterations.
